title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from pp. 41–43. K is a k-linear category with a universal cochain object 𝕀^· (written Č^· on p.42). Each x in K is 'located' by the cochain complex of k-modules α^·(x) = Hom(x, Č^·), with free finite-type terms. On p.42, β(C^i) is computed as a two-term complex (0→k→k→0), a 'disk' complex. This suggests K is the free k-linear (additive) category on a cochain complex, i.e. the 'walking complex'. Its objects then correspond, via α, to finite sums of contractible disk complexes, or at least sit inside bounded complexes of free f.t. modules.

Prop. 1 (earlier) says k-linear functors F: K → B correspond to cochain complexes in B, via F ↦ C_F^· = F(𝕀^·).

The question on this page is the inverse direction: given C^· in B^·, how do we compute F_C(x)? Prop. 3 answers with an isomorphism, bifunctorial in F and x:
F(x) ≅ Hom^·_k(α^·(x), F(𝕀^·)) = Hom^·_k(α^·(x), C_F^·).
This is a weighted limit (a Hom/end formula): the value at x is the limit of the diagram C_F^·, weighted by α^·(x).

The page then defines the B-valued Hom of a complex of k-modules into a complex in B. It is the object Hom^·_k(K^·, C^·) of B representing b ↦ Hom_{B^·}(b ⊗_k K^·, C^·). Here b ⊗_k K^i makes sense when the K^i are free of finite type, as finite direct sums of copies of b.

In general this is the kernel of δ: ∏_i Hom_k(K^i, C^i) → ∏_i Hom_k(K^i, C^{i+1}), with δ(u) = d u^i − u^{i+1} d. That kernel is the object of degree-0 chain maps, the Z^0 of the Hom complex. It is representable if:
- B has kernels;
- each Hom_k(K^i, C^i) is representable, e.g. K^i of finite presentation, or C^i^n for K^i free of rank n;
- the products exist, automatic when K^· is bounded (continued on p.44).

The proof (p.44) is the standard one:
- Build the canonical map F(x) ⊗ Hom(x, C^i) → F(C^i).
- Note that both sides are additive in x.
- Reduce to the generators x = C^i.
- There the map is the identity, by Yoneda.

Purpose. This is a Morita/Yoneda-type description of linear functors out of the walking-complex category. It feeds into the dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes, which is the subject of the cote.
errors: The double arrow '⇉' is used for the single map δ (equivalently, the kernel of the pair u ↦ du and u ↦ ud). This is harmless.
Representability of the infinite products is left open on this page. It is only needed for unbounded α^·(x), and the next page addresses it.
The phrase 'il se trouve qu'il l'est si K^· = ... ∈ Ob K^·' is garbled. Presumably it means representability holds when K^· is of the form α^·(x) (bounded, free of finite type).

ideas.what: Linear functors K→B from the walking-complex category correspond to cochain complexes in B; the value at x is recovered as Hom^·_k(α^·(x), C_F^·).
ideas.modern_name: Weighted limit / end formula; universal property of the free additive category on a complex (Yoneda/Morita for additive functors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of enriched category theory (Kelly, Street, 1970s); additive Morita theory (Mitchell, Freyd)

ideas.what: B-valued Hom from a complex of free f.t. k-modules into a complex in B, defined by representing b ↦ Hom_{B^·}(b⊗K^·, C^·), computed as the kernel of δ on ∏ Hom_k(K^i, C^i).
ideas.modern_name: Z^0 of the internal Hom complex; cotensor of a complex in B by a perfect complex of k-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homological algebra (Cartan–Eilenberg; cotensoring in additive categories)
ideas.where_published: Similar internal-Hom/tensor constructions with representability conditions appear in SGA 4 and SGA 6, but I am not sure of this exact form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Yoneda/weighted-limit computation inside a technical set-up. The mathematics is correct and standard, and nothing on the page appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'h-lin' and 'Hom_{h-l}(C, B)' are very likely 'k-lin' and 'Hom_{k-l}(K, B)' (k-linear functors from K).
'F(𝕀^·)' is the image of the universal cochain object (written Č^· on p.42), so C_F^· = F(𝕀^·).
The left margin note probably reads something like 'à mettre avant énoncé prop 3', not 'voir dans [?]'.
'B^·_k' in the bracketed definition should simply be B^· (cochain complexes in B).
